parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the centre of gravity of an object.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Two blocks are on a horizontal beam that is pivoted at its centre of gravity, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:fig_2_1}}

A large block of weight $54\text{ N}$ is a distance of $0.45\text{ m}$ from the pivot. A small block of weight $2.4\text{ N}$ is a distance of $0.95\text{ m}$ from the pivot and a distance of $0.35\text{ m}$ from the right-hand end of the beam.

The right-hand end of the beam is connected to the ground by a string that is at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. The beam is in equilibrium.
parts.text: By taking moments about the pivot, calculate the tension $T$ in the string.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.part_stem: The string is cut so that the beam is no longer in equilibrium.
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant moment about the pivot acting on the beam immediately after the string is cut.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the decrease in the gravitational potential energy of the block for its movement from X to Y.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer to (c)(i) and conservation of energy to determine the kinetic energy of the block at Y.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: State the variation, if any, in the direction of the acceleration of the block as it moves from X to Y.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.part_stem: The block passes point X at time $t_X$ and arrives at point Y at time $t_Y$.
